flags.note: The periphrastic construction 'and to him was the key' reflects Greek ἦν αὐτῷ. Native Hebrew would more likely use simple possession: וּמַפְתֵּחַ תְּהוֹם בְּיָדוֹ.
The purpose clause 'so that he could not' (ἵνα μή) is a direct Greek calque. Native Hebrew would use פֶּן or לְבִלְתִּי for negative purpose.
The passive construction 'and to them was given to judge' follows Greek καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς κρῖμα word order. Hebrew would prefer active voice or different passive construction.

flags.hebrew: אֵילּוּ הַמַּאֲמִינִים וּמְעִידִים... וְאֵילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא לָקְחוּ... וְאֵילּוּ חַיִּים
flags.note: The repetitive אֵילּוּ structures mirror Greek participial chains with καί connections. Hebrew would use more varied syntax.
The phrase 'no power from the second death' literally renders Greek οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος. Native Hebrew would express this concept differently.
The analytic genitive 'fire of Sheol' using שֶׁל reflects Greek influence. Standard Hebrew would use construct state: בְּאֵשׁ שְׁאוֹל.
The word order 'one throne great and white it was' follows Greek μέγαν λευκόν rather than natural Hebrew adjective placement.
The construction 'the dead, among them the small and the great' reflects Greek τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς μεγάλους καὶ τοὺς μικρούς structure rather than natural Hebrew.
